title: CARMENES an overview six months after first light
what_was_studied: Dual visible and near-infrared spectrographs, fibre feed, vacuum systems and early operation
numerical_result: VIS covers 520 to 960 nm and NIR 960 to 1710 nm at resolving power above 80000
remaining_question: A specification near 1 m/s is not a universal achieved precision for both channels

title: SERVAL SpEctrum Radial Velocity AnaLyser
what_was_studied: Template-matching velocities, differential line width, chromatic index and activity indicators
numerical_result: The method demonstrated m/s-scale differential velocities on high-resolution spectra; exact scatter depends on instrument, star and filtering
remaining_question: Pipeline comparisons require identical spectra, masks, zero points and uncertainty definitions

title: High-resolution optical and near-infrared spectroscopy of 324 survey stars
what_was_studied: Empirical Doppler information across spectral type and wavelength from more than 6500 observations
numerical_result: For M dwarfs the highest information generally occurred at 700 to 900 nm; longer wavelengths became competitive mainly for M8 to M9 stars
remaining_question: Information content predicts a statistical limit and does not include every telluric, calibration or activity term

title: Convective shift and starspot constraints from chromatic radial velocities
what_was_studied: Chromatic index and wavelength-dependent velocities used to constrain activity mechanisms
numerical_result: The study found that wavelength-dependent RV behaviour can distinguish spot and convective contributions in selected active stars
remaining_question: Transfer to quiet targets and planet-scale amplitudes requires star-specific validation

title: Guaranteed time observations Data Release 1 2016 to 2020
what_was_studied: Survey design, public spectra, high-level velocities and nightly zero-point corrections
numerical_result: DR1 contains 19633 spectra for 362 targets and 18642 precise RVs for 345 targets; median internal precision was 1.27 m/s
remaining_question: Internal uncertainty and target time-series RMS are different; nights without a direct zero point use adjacent-night estimates

title: The CARMENES search for exoplanets around M dwarfs precision of radial velocities
what_was_studied: Precision distribution and dependence on signal-to-noise and stellar properties across the released sample
numerical_result: Median internal precision was 1.6 m/s at median signal-to-noise 95 and scaled to 0.8 m/s at signal-to-noise 200
remaining_question: The scaled value is not a second achieved survey statistic and nightly zero points remain a separate term

title: Calar Alto autumn 2026 call for proposals
what_was_studied: Current open-time context for the 3.5 m telescope and its instruments
numerical_result: The call offers 3.5 m observing time in the July to December 2026 semester; the instrument page provides CARMENES observing instructions
remaining_question: The general call does not by itself document channel-specific downtime or every protected survey constraint
